title: Mates along an isomorphism of left adjoints
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C_i,\mathcal T_i)$ be triangulated categories with
$T_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_i$ the shifts, and let
$F_i:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_2$, $G_i:\mathcal C_2\to\mathcal C_1$
be exact functors with adjunctions
$F_1\dashv G_1$ (unit $\eta_1$, counit $\varepsilon_1$) and
$F_2\dashv G_2$ (unit $\eta_2$, counit $\varepsilon_2$), and let
$\alpha:F_1\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }F_2$ be a natural isomorphism.

1. There is a unique natural isomorphism
$\beta:G_1\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }G_2$ compatible with the adjunctions,
given explicitly by the composite
$$
\beta:\quad G_1
\xrightarrow{\ \eta_2G_1\ }
G_2F_2G_1
\xrightarrow{\ G_2\alpha^{-1}G_1\ }
G_2F_1G_1
\xrightarrow{\ G_2\varepsilon_1\ }
G_2
$$
and its inverse
$$
\beta^{-1}:\quad G_2
\xrightarrow{\ \eta_1G_2\ }
G_1F_1G_2
\xrightarrow{\ G_1\alpha G_2\ }
G_1F_2G_2
\xrightarrow{\ G_1\varepsilon_2\ }
G_1.
$$
1. The units and counits are carried to each other: the two
composite morphisms
$$
\operatorname{id}\xrightarrow{\ \eta_1\ }G_1F_1
\xrightarrow{\ \beta F_1\ }G_2F_1
\xrightarrow{\ G_2\alpha\ }G_2F_2,
\qquad
\operatorname{id}\xrightarrow{\ \eta_2\ }G_2F_2,
$$
are equal, and the two composites
$$
F_1G_1\xrightarrow{\ F_1\beta\ }F_1G_2
\xrightarrow{\ \alpha G_2\ }F_2G_2
\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon_2\ }\operatorname{id},
\qquad
F_1G_1\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon_1\ }\operatorname{id},
$$
are equal; the analogous identities hold with the roles of the two
adjunctions exchanged. In particular the unit-compatibility reads
$$
G_2\alpha\circ\beta F_1\circ\eta_1=\eta_2,
$$
as morphisms $\operatorname{id}\to G_2F_2$ after the canonical
identification $G_2F_1\xrightarrow{G_2\alpha}G_2F_2$.
1. *Uniqueness.* Any natural isomorphism
$\beta':G_1\xrightarrow{\sim}G_2$ satisfying the unit compatibility
of (2) together with its counit analogue is equal to $\beta$; in
particular the identification of $G_1$ with $G_2$ is canonical
once $\alpha$ is.

All functors and natural transformations are in the
classical framework.

proof.text: Apply the generic conjugation construction of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] to the two adjunctions with $L_1=F_1$, $R_1=G_1$, $L_2=F_2$, $R_2=G_2$ and the transformation $\tau=\alpha^{-1}:F_2\to F_1$. Its component formula is exactly $G_1\xrightarrow{\eta_2G_1}G_2F_2G_1\xrightarrow{G_2\alpha^{-1}G_1}G_2F_1G_1\xrightarrow{G_2\varepsilon_1}G_2$, so it defines $\beta:G_1\to G_2$. The same construction for $\alpha:F_1\to F_2$ gives the displayed $\beta^{-1}$; the bijection and inverse clauses of the cited statement show that these are inverse, and its isomorphism clause shows that $\beta$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: Hom-bijection construction and the two displayed mate formulas

proof.text: For the unit, expand the component of $\beta$ from Step 1 and compose it on the left with $\eta_1$. Naturality of $\eta_2$ and then of $\alpha^{-1}$ moves the two units through the first two factors; the triangle identity for $(F_1,G_1)$ cancels $G_2(\varepsilon_1F_1)$ with $G_2(F_1\eta_1)$, giving $\eta_1\,;\,\beta F_1=G_2(\alpha^{-1})\,;\,\eta_2$. Naturality of $\alpha$ rewrites this as $G_2(\alpha)\,;\,\beta F_1\,;\,\eta_1=\eta_2$, the first compatibility identity. For the inverse, expand $\beta^{-1}=G_1(\varepsilon_2);G_1(\alpha);\eta_1G_2$, use naturality of $\eta_1$ and $\alpha$, and cancel with the triangle identity for $(F_2,G_2)$; this gives $G_1(\alpha^{-1});\beta^{-1}F_2;\eta_2=\eta_1$.

For the counit, expand $\beta=G_2(\varepsilon_1);G_2(\alpha^{-1});\eta_2G_1$. Naturality of $\alpha^{-1}$ moves $F_2\beta$ past $\alpha^{-1}G_1$, and the triangle identity for $(F_2,G_2)$ then gives $\varepsilon_2;F_2\beta=\varepsilon_1;\alpha^{-1}$. Postcompose with $\alpha$ at $G_1(-)$ and use naturality of $\alpha$ for $\beta$ to obtain $\varepsilon_2;\alpha G_2;F_1\beta=\varepsilon_1$. For the inverse, expand $\beta^{-1}=G_1(\varepsilon_2);G_1(\alpha);\eta_1G_2$; naturality of $\alpha$ and the triangle identity for $(F_1,G_1)$ give $\varepsilon_1;\alpha^{-1}G_1;F_2\beta^{-1}=\varepsilon_2$. These are the two counit identities.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: counit compatibility and reversed identities

proof.text: Let $\beta':G_1\to G_2$ satisfy the stated unit compatibility (the additional counit compatibility is not needed). By the unit identity already proved for $\beta$, for every $c\in\mathcal C_1$ we have $\eta_{1,c};\beta'_{F_1c}=\eta_{1,c};\beta_{F_1c}$. For any $d\in\mathcal C_2$, naturality of $\beta'$ and the triangle identity for $(F_1,G_1)$ give $\beta'_d=G_2(\varepsilon_{1,d});\beta'_{F_1G_1d};\eta_{1,G_1d}$, and the identical expansion gives $\beta_d=G_2(\varepsilon_{1,d});\beta_{F_1G_1d};\eta_{1,G_1d}$. The equality at $c=G_1d$ therefore implies $\beta'_d=\beta_d$ for every $d$, so $\beta'=\beta$.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: uniqueness by the adjunction bijection/Yoneda

lean.statement: theorem adjointMate {C₁ : Type u₁} {C₂ : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁} C₁] [Category.{v₂} C₂] [Preadditive C₁] [Preadditive C₂] [HasZeroObject C₁] [HasZeroObject C₂] [HasShift C₁ ℤ] [HasShift C₂ ℤ] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C₁ n).Additive] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C₂ n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C₁] [Pretriangulated C₂] [IsTriangulated C₁] [IsTriangulated C₂] (F₁ F₂ : C₁ ⥤ C₂) (G₁ G₂ : C₂ ⥤ C₁) [F₁.CommShift ℤ] [F₂.CommShift ℤ] [G₁.CommShift ℤ] [G₂.CommShift ℤ] [F₁.IsTriangulated] [F₂.IsTriangulated] [G₁.IsTriangulated] [G₂.IsTriangulated] (adj₁ : F₁ ⊣ G₁) (adj₂ : F₂ ⊣ G₂) (α : F₁ ≅ F₂) : ∃ β : G₁ ≅ G₂, (∀ d : C₂, β.hom.app d = adj₂.unit.app (G₁.obj d) ≫ G₂.map (α.inv.app (G₁.obj d)) ≫ G₂.map (adj₁.counit.app d)) ∧ (∀ d : C₂, β.inv.app d = adj₁.unit.app (G₂.obj d) ≫ G₁.map (α.hom.app (G₂.obj d)) ≫ G₁.map (adj₂.counit.app d)) ∧ (∀ c : C₁, adj₁.unit.app c ≫ β.hom.app (F₁.obj c) ≫ G₂.map (α.hom.app c) = adj₂.unit.app c) ∧ (∀ d : C₂, F₁.map (β.hom.app d) ≫ α.hom.app (G₂.obj d) ≫ adj₂.counit.app d = adj₁.counit.app d) ∧ (∀ c : C₁, adj₂.unit.app c ≫ β.inv.app (F₂.obj c) ≫ G₁.map (α.inv.app c) = adj₁.unit.app c) ∧ (∀ d : C₂, F₂.map (β.inv.app d) ≫ α.inv.app (G₁.obj d) ≫ adj₁.counit.app d = adj₂.counit.app d) ∧ (∀ β' : G₁ ≅ G₂, (∀ c : C₁, adj₁.unit.app c ≫ β'.hom.app (F₁.obj c) ≫ G₂.map (α.hom.app c) = adj₂.unit.app c) → (∀ d : C₂, F₁.map (β'.hom.app d) ≫ α.hom.app (G₂.obj d) ≫ adj₂.counit.app d = adj₁.counit.app d) → β' = β)
